title: Minify the page: 512-bit sense slices with local wordline drivers
idea: MINIFY the activated page from 8 Kb to 512 bits: split each master wordline with local wordline drivers every 512 cells and gate sense-amp enable per slice using column address bits sent with ACT, so only the needed slice is charge-shared, sensed and restored.
why: Fact 8 (128x overfetch, ~5.9 pJ per useful bit): activation energy per useful bit drops ~10x and fewer bitlines swing near victims; cost ~3-4% area for extra local drivers.

title: Magnify sense time: integrating time-to-digital sensing for 1.5 fF cells
idea: MAGNIFY the sensing window from ~2 ns to 20-40 ns: after charge sharing, a constant-current integrator per bitline pair races both lines to a threshold and a shared counter (TDC) records which crosses first and by how much, resolving 5-10 mV differences a latch cannot.
why: Fact 1: tolerating ~3x less signal lets Cs fall from ~5 fF to ~1.5 fF, so pillar AR can fall from ~70:1 to ~25:1; added latency is hidden behind a row-buffer/SRAM tier for hot data.

title: Minify sense-amp count: one amplifier serially resolves eight held bitlines
idea: MINIFY the SA population 8x: bitlines are left floating after charge sharing (they hold the signal for ~100 ns as their own capacitors), and an 8:1 analog mux steps one larger, low-offset SA across them, each resolve-and-restore taking ~3 ns.
why: Fact 7 (periphery ~49%): SA stripe area -60-70%, periphery share toward ~40%; the larger shared SA also has lower offset; cost is ~20 ns longer row cycle.

title: Magnify signal ratio with a local gain transistor every 16 cells
idea: Hierarchical bitline: a 16-cell local bitline (~2-3 fF) drives the gate of one local amplifier transistor that conditionally discharges the long global bitline, MAGNIFYING the effective Cs/Cbl ratio from ~1:10 to ~1:1.
why: Facts 1-2: a 1-1.5 fF capacitor becomes readable, removing the AR wall and making short capacitors in 3D tiers viable; ~6-8% area spent on local amps.

title: Driven guard traces hide bitline coupling capacitance
idea: Borrow electrometer active guarding: MAGNIFY the role of shield lines between bitlines by driving each with a unity-gain follower of its neighbor bitline during charge sharing, so bitline-to-neighbor capacitance (~40% of Cbl) sees no voltage change and draws no charge.
why: Fact 1: effective Cbl -30-40%, signal +50-60%, allowing ~35% smaller Cs or lower VARY; followers are shared per 32 bitlines and only active for the ~2 ns window.

title: Sense-amp resolution time becomes soft information for row LDPC
idea: MINIFY sense margin almost to zero and MAGNIFY the code: each SA's latch-resolution time (slow = low confidence) is captured as a soft bit, and an 8 Kb row-level LDPC codeword (~3% parity) is decoded in the periphery, tolerating raw BER up to 1e-4.
why: Facts 1 and 10: permits VARY ~0.65 V (CV2 array energy -55%) and ~30% smaller Cs; soft information roughly halves parity versus hard-decision codes.

title: Vacuum-sealed cavities around bitlines minify parasitic capacitance
idea: MAGNIFY the air-spacer idea into a fully sealed vacuum tunnel: bitlines are suspended between storage-node contacts on periodic posts, a sacrificial carbon fill is ashed out, and a pinch-off dielectric seals the cavity, giving k~1 on three sides.
why: Fact 1: Cbl -45-50% versus nitride spacers, doubling signal so pillar height (and AR) can drop ~40%; also cuts bitline switching energy.

title: Thousand-point on-die thermal map sets per-mat refresh
idea: MAGNIFY temperature sensing from 1-2 sensors per die to one ~50 um2 ring-oscillator thermometer per mat (~1,000 per die), and scale each mat's refresh interval to its local temperature, since leakage doubles roughly every 10 C.
why: Fact 3: in HBM stacks with 10-20 C gradients, refresh energy and bandwidth loss fall ~30-50%; area cost <0.1%.

title: Half-size canary capacitors trigger subarray refresh on demand
idea: MINIFY a few sentinel cells on purpose: each 512-row subarray carries 8 canary cells with half-size capacitors and deliberately leaky access devices; a low-power comparator polls them and refreshes the subarray only when a canary decays below threshold.
why: Fact 3: refresh tracks actual retention instead of the 13 fA worst-case tail, cutting refresh operations 4-10x at typical temperatures.

title: Leaky-capacitor analog activation counter per row stops row hammer
idea: MINIFY the row-hammer tracker from multi-KB SRAM count tables to ~2 transistors and one tiny capacitor per wordline driver: each ACT pumps in a fixed charge packet, a calibrated leak drains it with a ~64 ms time constant, and crossing threshold raises a neighbor-refresh request.
why: Fact 9 (flips at ~1k activations): exact per-row tracking for ~1% periphery area instead of probabilistic sampling, with no counter SRAM.

title: Evict charge pumps: package PMIC supplies VPP to sixteen dies
idea: MINIFY on-die high-voltage generation to zero: one ~85%-efficient switched-inductor PMIC on the HBM base die or DIMM generates VPP/VBB for all dies and delivers them on dedicated TSVs or balls, replacing on-die capacitive pumps.
why: Facts 7 and 10: removes pump capacitors and oscillators (~3-5% of die) and raises VPP efficiency from ~30% to ~85%, cutting wall-plug wordline energy ~2.5x.

title: Magnify mat size with mid-bitline charge-transfer preamplifiers
idea: MAGNIFY bitlines from 512 to 2,048 cells by inserting a charge-transfer (Heller-type PMOS) preamplifier at the midpoint that moves far-segment charge onto a small node with gain, halving the number of SA stripes and decoder columns per bit.
why: Fact 7: SA plus decoder overhead per bit -25-30%, periphery share toward ~38%; a 1990s trick reused for a periphery-bound era.

title: Quarter-size sense amps with one-time digital offset trim
idea: MINIFY SA transistors 4x and accept ~40 mV offset; at wafer test, measure each SA's offset and store a 4-bit code in a dense trim array that drives a small capacitive DAC on the latch node during every sense.
why: Fact 7: SA area -50% while effective offset returns to <5 mV, which in turn tolerates smaller Cs (Fact 1).

title: SiGe HBT preamps exploit bipolar matching for tiny signals
idea: MAGNIFY matching precision by switching device physics: one SiGe heterojunction-bipolar differential preamp per 16 bitlines (Vbe mismatch ~1 mV versus 10-20 mV for minimum MOS) amplifies the signal before a CMOS latch.
why: Facts 1 and 10: resolves ~10 mV in ~1 ns, allowing ~3x smaller Cs or VARY ~0.6 V; BiCMOS DRAM died on cost, but periphery on a separate bonded wafer removes that penalty.

title: Room-temperature single-electron electrometers read 300-electron cells
idea: MINIFY the stored charge 100x: sub-2 nm metal or Si-nanocrystal single-electron transistors gate-coupled to short local bitlines sense ~50 aC (about 300 electrons), so the storage capacitor shrinks to ~0.05 fF and the tall pillar disappears.
why: Facts 1-2: eliminates the capacitor wall and enables thin planar 3D tiers, potentially 3-5x density; room-temperature SET uniformity is unproven.

title: Shift-register row sequencer replaces decoders in streaming banks
idea: MINIFY the row decoder in designated stream banks to a circular shift register that advances one wordline per ACT plus a coarse 1-of-16 jump decoder, since AI weight and KV streams open rows in order; random traffic is steered to normal banks.
why: Fact 7: decoder area -80% and decode energy -70% in stream banks; ~5-8% die saved if half the banks stream.

title: Radio-frequency tone addressing selects wordline groups via resonators
idea: MINIFY decoder wiring to a single line: the row address is broadcast as a sum of on-die RF tones, and each wordline-driver group has a tuned LC or MEMS resonator filter bank that fires only when its tone combination is present.
why: Fact 7: replaces predecode buses and NAND decode trees (several % of die) with one global line; selectivity and latency make this speculative.

title: Successive-approximation sense amp magnifies bits per capacitor
idea: MAGNIFY bits per cell to two: after charge sharing, a 3-step successive-approximation sense amp with a capacitive DAC shared among 4 bitlines resolves four charge levels and writes back the quantized level during restore.
why: Facts 1 and 4: doubles bits per capacitor for ~1.3x SA area, a cost-per-bit gain worth ~2 nodes; risky because each level keeps only ~1/3 of the margin.

title: Frozen periphery platform wafer reused for three array generations
idea: Hybrid-bond each new array wafer onto a standardized 28 nm periphery wafer whose bond interface and protocol are frozen for 6+ years, so a new node needs only array masks: MAGNIFY the periphery's lifetime, MINIFY per-node mask and EUV spend.
why: Facts 4 and 7: per-node capex -30-40%; periphery wafers can come from existing U.S. trailing-edge fabs, raising U.S. content.

title: One shared SerDes chiplet replaces eight dies' wide PHYs
idea: MINIFY each DRAM die's PHY, DLL and I/O ring (~8-10% of area) to a narrow on-package bridge port, and MAGNIFY a single 224G SerDes chiplet that serializes traffic for eight dies.
why: Fact 7: ~8% of die area returned to cells and fewer pins per bit; like a CXL buffer but pulled inside the package.

title: Switched-capacitor bitline doubler magnifies signal before latching
idea: After charge sharing, switches reconnect the two halves of each bitline pair in series (a switched-capacitor voltage doubler), MAGNIFYING the differential signal ~1.8x before the latch fires, which lets VARY MINIFY to ~0.5-0.6 V.
why: Fact 10: CV2 array energy -65%; alternatively relaxes Cs ~40% (Fact 1).

title: Thirty-two-cell averaged reference minifies reference error
idea: MAGNIFY the reference: each mat's sense reference is generated by charge-averaging 32 dummy cells written half 0 and half 1 at every refresh, so it tracks process, temperature and leakage with sqrt(32) less random error than a single dummy.
why: Fact 1: recovers ~20-30% of sense margin, convertible into smaller Cs or longer refresh intervals (Fact 3).

title: Skip restore for read-once data like KV-cache streams
idea: MINIFY restore work: a read-and-forget command lets the SA latch the row without driving restore current back into the cells, and the controller marks the row invalid, for data consumed once (streamed activations, KV pages being evicted).
why: Fact 8: restore is ~40-50% of activation energy and time; skipping it raises effective bandwidth and reduces disturbance to neighbors.

title: Periphery evicted upstairs: oxide-tellurium CMOS sense amps over array
idea: Within a 400 C budget, build sense amps and decoders in BEOL tiers directly above the cell array using n-type IGZO (deposited ~300 C) and p-type tellurium TFTs (evaporated near room temperature), MINIFYING periphery footprint on silicon toward zero.
why: Fact 7: periphery share of die from ~49% to ~15%, ~1.6x bits per wafer; tellurium p-FET stability is the main risk.

title: Ferroelectric HZO negative-capacitance shunt minifies effective bitline capacitance
idea: A thin HZO film (crystallized at 350-400 C) in a capacitor shunted to each bitline segment is biased in its negative-capacitance region during charge sharing, MINIFYING the net bitline capacitance by 50-70%.
why: Fact 1: signal 2-3x, enabling ~2x smaller Cs or VARY ~0.6 V; hysteresis-free transient NC at ns speed is unproven, hence high risk.

title: NEMS relay wordline drivers with zero off-leakage
idea: Ruthenium-contact nanoelectromechanical relays are built in BEOL at <=350 C with a sacrificial release and used as mat-select and wordline-driver switches: they pass 3 V natively, need no level shifters or stacked high-voltage transistors, and leak nothing when open.
why: Facts 7 and 10: wordline-driver area MINIFIED 2-3x and standby leakage to ~0, tungsten-free; contact wear and ~10 ns mechanical delay are the risks.

title: IGZO shadow row buffers magnify open rows eightfold
idea: Stack 2T0C IGZO gain-cell latches (<=350 C; leakage <1e-18 A, so they hold for seconds) above each SA stripe, giving every bank 8 shadow row buffers that keep recently opened rows readable without re-activation.
why: Facts 8 and 9: activations fall ~30-50% for AI access patterns, cutting overfetch energy and row-hammer exposure, with zero added silicon area.

title: Remanent-polarization offset trim inside each sense latch
idea: Place a tiny AlScN or HZO ferroelectric capacitor (both <=400 C) on each SA latch node and partially polarize it at test so its remanent charge cancels that SA's offset, MINIFYING offset to near zero with no trim SRAM or DAC.
why: Fact 7: SA transistors can shrink ~4x; the trim is nonvolatile and can be re-set in the field as devices age.

title: N-type-only oxide sense amp using capacitive bootstrapping
idea: MINIFY the device menu to one transistor type: an IGZO-only cross-coupled latch uses bootstrapped capacitive pull-ups (as in display gate drivers) instead of p-FETs, avoiding immature p-type oxides and keeping the periphery tier to ~8 masks at <=350 C.
why: Facts 4 and 7: a mask-light, EUV-free periphery tier above the array; ~2-3x slower than Si SAs, offset by sensing more columns in parallel.

title: SiN photonic H-tree replaces the die's global data wires
idea: PECVD silicon-nitride waveguides (<=350 C), electro-optic polymer ring modulators (cured <=200 C) and sputtered polycrystalline Ge detectors form an optical global bus from banks to I/O, MAGNIFYING bandwidth per wire ~20x.
why: Fact 5: on-die global data-movement energy from ~1 pJ/bit to ~0.2 pJ/bit with far fewer global wires; low-temperature poly-Ge responsivity is the risk.

title: Charge-pump capacitors move into six BEOL MIM levels
idea: ALD ZrO2/HfO2 MIM capacitors (250-300 C) stacked in six upper metal levels MAGNIFY pump capacitance per footprint ~6x, so pumps run at lower frequency with higher efficiency and their silicon area is freed for cells.
why: Facts 7 and 10: ~3-4% die area reclaimed and VPP efficiency +15-20 points.

title: Ovonic threshold switch acts as one-device bitline comparator
idea: A room-temperature-sputtered chalcogenide OTS is biased just below threshold; the charge-shared bitline from a '1' pushes it over, and its snap-back delivers a large current pulse (near-infinite gain) captured by a 2-TFT latch, MINIFYING a ~12-transistor SA to ~3 devices.
why: Fact 7: SA area -70%; OTS threshold spread (~50 mV) must be trimmed per device, hence high risk.

title: BEOL Schottky diode-matrix decoders minify predecode transistors
idea: Pd/IGZO Schottky diodes (<=300 C) wired as diode-ROM one-hot decoders above the array replace transistor predecoders, MINIFYING decoder transistor count ~10x and moving decode logic off the silicon.
why: Fact 7: row and column decoder silicon area -70%; reverse leakage in large fan-in diode matrices sets the size limit.

title: Active glass interposer with IGZO switches routes around bad dies
idea: MAGNIFY redundancy from cells to whole dies: a glass interposer carries IGZO TFT switch matrices (<=350 C) that remap channels from a failing HBM die or TSV column to a spare die in the stack, configured at final test.
why: Fact 6: recovers much of the 20-30% HBM stack yield loss; glass panel substrates are cheap and a U.S. manufacturing strength.

title: Back-gate-pulsed dual-gate IGZO sense amplifiers
idea: Dual-gate IGZO SA transistors (<=350 C) get their back gate pulsed to +2 V only during the ~2-3 ns sense window, MAGNIFYING drive current ~3x, and parked at -1 V otherwise, MINIFYING leakage.
why: Facts 3 and 10: closes most of the oxide-versus-Si speed gap for over-array SAs while keeping periphery standby leakage near zero.

title: Resonant clock grid with electroplated copper inductors
idea: Thick electroplated Cu spiral inductors (<=250 C) in top metal resonate with the periphery clock-grid capacitance, recycling clock energy each cycle instead of dumping it, MINIFYING clock and DLL power.
why: Fact 5: clock power -40%, worth ~5-8% of DRAM interface power; uses only mature low-temperature steps.

title: Dirac-source steep-slope sense transistors at 0.4 V
idea: Low-temperature (<=400 C) MOCVD MoS2 channels with a graphene cold-source contact that filters out high-energy electrons give sub-60 mV/decade switching, letting SAs and the array MINIFY VARY to ~0.4 V.
why: Fact 10: CV2 array energy -80%; low-temperature 2D growth quality and contact resistance make it speculative.

title: Per-driver BEOL bootstrap capacitor self-boosts every wordline
idea: Each wordline driver gets a local high-k MIM bootstrap capacitor (<=300 C) that capacitively lifts the selected wordline above VDD at the moment of selection, MINIFYING the global VPP network and its pump to a small reserve.
why: Facts 7 and 10: VPP distribution and pump area -60%, wordline energy -30% because only the selected line is boosted.

title: BEOL MTJ repair registers replace laser and eFuse banks
idea: MINIFY redundancy fuse area ~10x by storing repair addresses in BEOL magnetic tunnel junctions (annealed <=400 C) instead of laser fuses or eFuses, and MAGNIFY repair opportunities by reprogramming them in the field after aging or row-hammer damage.
why: Fact 7 (fuse banks and repair logic are several % of periphery) plus lifetime yield: weak rows can be swapped for spares over the product life.

title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode latch as two-terminal sense amplifier
idea: Revive the 1959 Goto pair: two ALD MIM resonant-tunneling (negative-differential-resistance) diodes in series form a bistable node; the bitline nudges the midpoint and a clock pulse latches it, MINIFYING the SA to two diodes plus one access TFT, all <=300 C.
why: Fact 7: SA area -70-80% if a peak-to-valley ratio >3 can be reached in low-temperature MIM stacks; device physics is speculative.

title: IGZO charge-coupled readout drains rows to few sense nodes
idea: MAGNIFY serialization: like a CCD image sensor, a row's charge packets are shifted bucket-brigade along BEOL IGZO transfer gates (<=350 C) to one floating-diffusion sense node per 64 columns, MINIFYING sense amps 64x for sequential tensor streams.
why: Fact 7: periphery area in stream banks -50%; IGZO's tiny leakage keeps packets intact during transfer, but transfer inefficiency is the risk.

title: Inductive coupling coils replace TSVs between stacked dies
idea: MINIFY TSVs to zero for data: copper coils in each die's top BEOL (<=250 C) couple signals inductively to the dies above and below (ThruChip-style), so stacks need no TSV etch, fill or keep-out zones for data.
why: Fact 6: removes much of the TSV area tax and stack yield loss; power still needs a few TSVs or edge delivery.

title: Tungsten-free periphery contacts using ALD molybdenum and ruthenium
idea: MINIFY tungsten to zero in SA and decoder contacts and local interconnect by depositing Mo or Ru at <=400 C by ALD/CVD, which also lowers contact resistance at small dimensions.
why: Scarce resource (China ~80% of tungsten): removes a chokepoint from periphery; lower resistance speeds narrow periphery wiring.

title: Minify the fab: 400 C-only periphery add-on lines in U.S.
idea: Build $1-2B BEOL-only lines (no furnaces, epi, implanters or EUV) near U.S. packaging sites that add IGZO periphery, row-buffer and repair tiers onto array wafers bought from any supplier, capturing roughly half of die value domestically.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: ~1/8 the capex of a full DRAM fab and ~18-month build versus 3-5 years.

title: Stepwise tank-capacitor charging makes bitline restore nearly adiabatic
idea: MAGNIFY on-die charge storage: bitline restore and equalization proceed in 4 steps through BEOL high-k tank capacitors (<=300 C) instead of one full swing from the supply, so each step dissipates only ~1/4 of the CV2/2 that a direct swing wastes.
why: Facts 8 and 10: array activation energy -25-35% without lowering voltages.

title: Accumulative ferroelectric FET counts activations per row nonvolatilely
idea: Exploit accumulative partial switching in HZO/AlScN: each ACT applies a sub-coercive pulse to a per-row FeFET (<=400 C), nudging its threshold one step; after N steps it trips a neighbor-refresh flag and is reset, MINIFYING a row-hammer counter to one transistor.
why: Fact 9: exact per-row counts at ~0.5% area with no SRAM tables; FeFET endurance (~1e10 cycles) versus reset rate is the main risk.
